notes: Stream-integrated planning stage. Step 1 is a MANDATORY input-contract: detect the source of truth (priority requirements/SRS.md -> brainstorm/BRAINSTORM.md -> research/RES-*.md -> code), ASK the user which to plan from when several exist, and REFUSE to plan on nothing. Writes docs/streams/[feature]-[YYYYMMDD]/plan/PLAN.md; opens the stream STREAM-LIGHT (lane: brownfield, no forced REQUIREMENT/DESIGN) when none exists, making it the brownfield entry-point. Evaluate that: greenfield is not regressed (SRS still consumed first); brownfield code-only plans from code and opens a stream-light stream; a research report is a valid source; empty input is refused (no fabricated scope); multiple sources trigger a user-selectable ask (not auto-pick). The end-to-end delivery boundary should still NOT fire, since delivery is a sequence of separately gated stages.

evals.prompt: We have an approved SRS for the order-export feature at docs/streams/order-export-20260804/requirements/SRS.md. Write the implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: greenfield-no-regression. Step 1 detects requirements/SRS.md as the (single, top-priority) source of truth and plans directly from it — no ask needed. Produces a one-screen docs/streams/order-export-20260804/plan/PLAN.md: phase/task table naming specific files/endpoints, done-conditions, explicit dependencies, status values; states the source of truth was the SRS. Updates STREAM.md membership row + board. Does NOT regress the brainstorm->SRS->plan flow.

evals.prompt: This existing repo has no CBR docs. Plan the work to add pagination to the existing product-list API.
evals.expected_output: brownfield code-only. Step 1 finds no SRS/brainstorm/research; the source of truth is the code, so it scouts the relevant modules (Glob/Grep) before decomposing. Since no stream exists, it OPENS ONE STREAM-LIGHT: creates docs/streams/<slug>-<YYYYMMDD>/, scaffolds STREAM.md from the shipped STREAM template with lane: brownfield, copies the derived Gate Status zone verbatim (authors no gate values), and does NOT write an SRS/design or force REQUIREMENT/DESIGN. Writes plan/PLAN.md with tasks naming real files. Ends and stops (no cascade to implement-feature).

evals.prompt: There's a research report at docs/streams/search-revamp-20260804/research/RES-search-internals.md and no SRS yet. Plan the search-revamp work from it.
evals.expected_output: research-fed. Step 1 detects research/RES-*.md as the highest-priority source present (no SRS/brainstorm) and plans from it — reuses the existing research artifact as a valid source of truth (no new artifact type invented). Writes docs/streams/search-revamp-20260804/plan/PLAN.md into the existing stream, states RES was the source, updates STREAM.md.

evals.prompt: Plan the work for our new billing system.
evals.expected_output: refuse-on-empty. Step 1 finds no SRS, no brainstorm, no research report, and no code it has been pointed at to plan against. It REFUSES to plan on nothing rather than fabricating scope — tells the user to run the explore/scout skill or the researcher agent first to produce a research/RES-*.md, or start with brainstorming if the direction is not yet decided. Writes no PLAN.md and invents no requirements.

evals.prompt: Plan the checkout-refactor. The stream has both requirements/SRS.md and research/RES-checkout-audit.md present.
evals.expected_output: multi-SoT user-selectable. Step 1 detects MORE THAN ONE source of truth (SRS + research report). It does NOT silently apply the priority order and auto-pick the SRS — it lists what it found and ASKS the user which to plan from (AskUserQuestion, pre-analyzed options grounded in the files on disk), optionally letting them pick a primary source and fold the other in as a constraint. Only after the user chooses does it write plan/PLAN.md, recording the chosen source.

evals.prompt: Take the login feature from requirements all the way through design, implementation, and tests end to end.
evals.expected_output: delivery-boundary negative — should NOT fire, because this asks for end-to-end feature delivery across all SDLC stages, not just writing the plan artifact. Correct response names the stage sequence (analyze-requirement, then design-screen/design-function, then implement-feature, then unit-test/integration-test) and starts at the first one — each stage gates on user approval, so nothing runs the whole chain.
